name: Diethylene glycol monohexyl ether
description: Diethylene glycol monohexyl ether (CAS 112-59-4 ), also known commercially as Hexyl Carbitol, is a slow-evaporating glycol ether solvent used across coatings, cleaning, and metalworking formulations. Its combination of hydrophilic and lipophilic character makes it effective as both a solvent carrier and an emulsifier in water-based and solvent-based systems. In architectural and industrial coatings, it functions as a coalescing aid. It serves as a coupling solvent, improving film formation and flow in waterborne latex paints. Printing ink formulators use it to control viscosity and drying rate in packaging inks, particularly where extended open time is required. In metalworking and industrial cleaning compounds, it acts as a degreasing solvent and emulsifier, helping to lift and disperse oils from metal surfaces. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it as a reactive diluent. It is used as a processing solvent to adjust application viscosity without compromising final bond strength. This versatile chemical is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities for industrial use. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher. Specifications are aligned with industrial solvent requirements, and material is generally available with standard COA documentation. The documentation covers purity, water content, and color to ensure consistency. This product meets the rigorous demands of chemical manufacturing and large-scale industrial applications across various global markets.
